ei.title: 강한 의견보다 중요한 것: 사실에 근거한 주장의 힘
ei.subject: 수능특강Light

fullPassage: There is no problem with people having strong opinions. On the contrary, it’s important that they do and that they argue for them vigorously. However, people’s opinions should always be fact based. Insisting that decision making be fact driven doesn’t detract from the importance of opinions. It just means people are expected to try really hard to make sure theirs are well founded. I often say to executives, “Have an opinion; take a stand; be right most of the time.” Opinions aren’t helpful unless the people who hold them are willing to take a stand in their defense by making a fact-based case. One of the great dangers in business is people who are great at winning an argument due to their powers of persuasion rather than the merits of their case.

questions.passage: There is no problem with people having (A)[weak / strong] opinions. On the contrary, it’s (B)[trivial / important] that they do and that they argue for them vigorously. However, people’s opinions should always be fact based. Insisting that decision making be fact driven doesn’t detract from the importance of opinions. It just means people are expected to try really hard to make sure theirs are well founded. I often say to executives, “Have an opinion; take a stand; be right most of the time.” Opinions aren’t (C)[helpful / useless] unless the people who hold them are willing to take a stand in their defense by making a fact-based case. One of the great dangers in business is people who are great at winning an argument due to their powers of persuasion rather than the merits of their case.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① strong — important — helpful

(A) strong(강한): 첫 문장은 사람들이 '강한' 의견을 갖는 것은 문제가 없다는 내용이에요. weak(약한)는 글의 전제와 반대예요.

(B) important(중요한): 오히려 의견을 갖고 활기차게 주장하는 것이 '중요하다'고 이어져요. trivial(하찮은)은 뒤의 argue for them vigorously와 모순이에요.

(C) helpful(도움이 되는): 의견은 사실 근거로 옹호할 때에만 '도움이 된다'는 맥락이에요. useless(쓸모없는)는 unless(~하지 않는 한) 구문의 논리를 깨뜨려요.
det.tip: strong(강한) ↔ weak(약한), important(중요한) ↔ trivial(하찮은), helpful(도움이 되는) ↔ useless(쓸모없는)

questions.passage: There is no problem with people having strong opinions. On the contrary, it’s (A)[trivial / important] that they do and that they argue for them vigorously. However, people’s opinions should always be fact based. Insisting that decision making be fact driven doesn’t detract from the importance of opinions. It just means people are expected to try really hard to make sure theirs are well founded. I often say to executives, “Have an opinion; take a stand; be right most of the time.” Opinions aren’t helpful unless the people who hold them are (B)[reluctant / willing] to take a stand in their defense by making a fact-based case. One of the great (C)[dangers / benefits] in business is people who are great at winning an argument due to their powers of persuasion rather than the merits of their case.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ important — willing — dangers

(A) important(중요한): 의견을 갖고 주장하는 것이 '중요하다'는 도입이에요. trivial(하찮은)은 흐름과 반대예요.

(B) willing(기꺼이 하는): 의견은 그것을 가진 사람이 '기꺼이' 나서서 옹호할 때 유용해요. reluctant(꺼리는)는 unless 뒤 조건과 모순이에요.

(C) dangers(위험): 설득력만으로 이기는 사람은 사업의 큰 '위험'이라는 부정적 평가예요. benefits(이익)는 글쓴이의 경계하는 태도와 정반대예요.
det.tip: important ↔ trivial, willing(기꺼이) ↔ reluctant(꺼리는), dangers(위험) ↔ benefits(이익)

questions.passage: There is no problem with people having strong opinions. On the contrary, it’s important that they do and that they argue for them (A)[reluctantly / vigorously]. However, people’s opinions should always be fact based. Insisting that decision making be fact driven doesn’t detract from the importance of opinions. It just means people are expected to try really hard to make sure theirs are well founded. I often say to executives, “Have an opinion; take a stand; be right most of the time.” Opinions aren’t (B)[useless / helpful] unless the people who hold them are willing to take a stand in their defense by making a fact-based case. One of the great dangers in business is people who are great at winning an argument due to their powers of persuasion rather than the (C)[merits / faults] of their case.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② vigorously — helpful — merits

(A) vigorously(활기차게): 의견을 '활기차게(강력하게)' 주장하는 것이 중요하다는 맥락이에요. reluctantly(마지못해)는 important와 어울리지 않아요.

(B) helpful(도움이 되는): 사실 근거로 옹호할 때에만 의견이 '도움이 된다'는 흐름이에요. useless(쓸모없는)는 문장 논리를 뒤집어요.

(C) merits(진가/장점): 설득력이 아니라 주장 자체의 '진가'로 이겨야 한다는 대비예요. faults(결점)는 rather than(~보다는)의 대비 논리와 맞지 않아요.
det.tip: vigorously(활기차게) ↔ reluctantly(마지못해), merits(진가) ↔ faults(결점)

questions.passage: There is no problem with people having strong opinions. On the contrary, it’s ①<u>important</u> that they do and that they argue for them vigorously. However, people’s opinions should always be fact based. Insisting that decision making be fact driven doesn’t detract from the importance of opinions. It just means people are expected to try really ②<u>hard</u> to make sure theirs are well founded. I often say to executives, “Have an opinion; take a stand; be right most of the time.” Opinions aren’t ③<u>helpful</u> unless the people who hold them are willing to take a stand in their defense by making a fact-based case. One of the great ④<u>advantages</u> in business is people who are great at winning an argument due to their powers of persuasion rather than the merits of their case.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① important(중요한): 의견을 갖고 주장하는 것이 중요하다 — 적절해요.

✅ ② hard(열심히): try really hard(정말 열심히 노력하다) — 적절해요.

✅ ③ helpful(도움이 되는): 사실로 옹호할 때 의견이 도움이 된다 — 적절해요.

❌ ④ advantages(이점): 원문은 dangers(위험)예요. 설득력만으로 이기는 사람은 사업에서 경계해야 할 '위험'이지 '이점'이 아니에요. 글쓴이의 부정적 평가와 정반대라 부적절해요. ←정답
det.tip: dangers(위험) ↔ advantages(이점) — 글쓴이가 경계하는 대상이므로 부정적 단어가 맞아요.

questions.passage: There is no problem with people having strong opinions. On the contrary, it’s important that they do and that they argue for them vigorously. However, people’s opinions should ①<u>always</u> be fact based. Insisting that decision making be fact driven doesn’t detract from the ②<u>triviality</u> of opinions. It just means people are ③<u>expected</u> to try really hard to make sure theirs are well founded. I often say to executives, “Have an opinion; take a stand; be right most of the time.” Opinions aren’t helpful unless the people who hold them are ④<u>willing</u> to take a stand in their defense by making a fact-based case. One of the great dangers in business is people who are great at winning an argument due to their powers of persuasion rather than the merits of their case.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① always(항상): 의견은 '항상' 사실에 근거해야 한다 — 적절해요.

❌ ② triviality(하찮음): 원문은 importance(중요성)예요. 사실에 근거해 결정하자는 주장이 의견의 '중요성'을 깎아내리지 않는다는 흐름인데, '하찮음을 깎아내리지 않는다'는 말은 앞뒤가 맞지 않아요. ←정답

✅ ③ expected(기대되는): 사람들이 노력하도록 기대된다 — 적절해요.

✅ ④ willing(기꺼이 하는): 기꺼이 나서서 옹호한다 — 적절해요.
det.tip: detract from the importance of ~: ~의 중요성을 깎아내리다 (importance ↔ triviality)

questions.passage: There is no problem with people having strong opinions. On the contrary, it’s important that they do and that they argue for them ①<u>vigorously</u>. However, people’s opinions should always be fact based. Insisting that decision making be fact driven doesn’t ②<u>detract</u> from the importance of opinions. It just means people are expected to try really hard to make sure theirs are well founded. I often say to executives, “Have an opinion; take a stand; be right most of the time.” Opinions aren’t helpful unless the people who hold them are willing to take a stand in their defense by making a fact-based case. One of the great dangers in business is people who are great at ③<u>losing</u> an argument due to their powers of ④<u>persuasion</u> rather than the merits of their case.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① vigorously(활기차게): 의견을 활기차게 주장한다 — 적절해요.

✅ ② detract(깎아내리다): 중요성을 깎아내리지 않는다 — 적절해요.

❌ ③ losing(지는): 원문은 winning(이기는)이에요. 뒤에 '설득력(powers of persuasion) 때문에'가 이어지는데, 설득력은 논쟁에서 '이기게' 하는 힘이지 '지게' 하는 힘이 아니에요. ←정답

✅ ④ persuasion(설득): powers of persuasion(설득력) — 적절해요.
det.tip: winning an argument(논쟁에서 이기기) ↔ losing(지기). 설득력은 '이김'과 연결돼요.

questions.passage: There is no problem with people having strong opinions. On the contrary, it’s important that they do and that they argue for them __________. However, people’s opinions should always be fact based. Insisting that decision making be fact driven doesn’t detract from the importance of opinions. It just means people are expected to try really hard to make sure theirs are well founded. I often say to executives, “Have an opinion; take a stand; be right most of the time.” Opinions aren’t helpful unless the people who hold them are willing to take a stand in their defense by making a fact-based case. One of the great dangers in business is people who are great at winning an argument due to their powers of persuasion rather than the merits of their case.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① vigorously(활기차게): 의견을 갖는 것이 중요하고, 또 그것을 '활기차게' 주장하는 것이 중요하다는 흐름이에요.

❌ ② silently(조용히): 주장(argue)한다는 동사와 어울리지 않아요.

❌ ③ carelessly(부주의하게): 뒤에 나오는 '사실 근거' 강조와 모순이에요.

❌ ④ rarely(거의 ~않게): 주장이 중요하다는 맥락과 반대예요.
det.tip: vigorously: 활기차게, 힘차게 (argue vigorously = 강력하게 주장하다)

questions.passage: There is no problem with people having strong opinions. On the contrary, it’s important that they do and that they argue for them vigorously. However, people’s opinions should always be fact based. Insisting that decision making be fact driven doesn’t __________ from the importance of opinions. It just means people are expected to try really hard to make sure theirs are well founded. I often say to executives, “Have an opinion; take a stand; be right most of the time.” Opinions aren’t helpful unless the people who hold them are willing to take a stand in their defense by making a fact-based case. One of the great dangers in business is people who are great at winning an argument due to their powers of persuasion rather than the merits of their case.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ detract(깎아내리다): 사실에 근거해 결정하자는 주장이 의견의 중요성을 '깎아내리지' 않는다는 뜻이에요. detract from ~ = ~을 손상시키다/깎아내리다.

❌ ① benefit(이득을 얻다): '중요성으로부터 이득을 얻지 않는다'는 어색해요.

❌ ② suffer(고통받다): 문맥과 무관해요.

❌ ④ result(결과로 생기다): result from은 '~에서 비롯되다'라 의미가 맞지 않아요.
det.tip: detract from ~: ~을 깎아내리다, 손상시키다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② willing(기꺼이 하는): 의견을 가진 사람이 '기꺼이' 나서서 사실 근거로 옹호할 때에만 의견이 유용하다는 맥락이에요. be willing to ~ = 기꺼이 ~하다.

❌ ① afraid(두려워하는): 나서서 옹호한다는 능동적 태도와 반대예요.

❌ ③ forced(강요받는): 자발적 태도(기꺼이)와 어긋나요.

❌ ④ unable(할 수 없는): 옹호에 나선다는 내용과 모순이에요.
det.tip: be willing to + 동사원형: 기꺼이 ~하다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 helpful과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① useful(유용한): helpful(도움이 되는)과 동의어예요.

❌ ② harmful(해로운): 반의어예요.

❌ ③ careless(부주의한): 의미가 달라요.

❌ ④ expensive(비싼): 무관한 의미예요.
det.tip: helpful = useful = beneficial(도움이 되는)

questions.passage: There is no problem with people having strong opinions. On the contrary, it’s important that they do and that they argue for them vigorously. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 detract와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ④ diminish(줄이다, 약화시키다): detract(깎아내리다)와 가장 가까워요. detract from the importance = 중요성을 약화시키다.

❌ ① announce(발표하다): 무관해요.

❌ ② organize(조직하다): 무관해요.

❌ ③ celebrate(기념하다): 의미가 달라요.
det.tip: detract from = diminish = reduce(줄이다, 깎아내리다)

questions.passage: There is no problem with people having strong opinions. On the contrary, it’s important that they do and that they argue for them vigorously. However, people’s opinions should always be fact based. Insisting that decision making be fact driven doesn’t detract from the importance of opinions. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 merits와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ④ strengths(강점): 여기서 merits는 주장 '자체가 지닌 진가/강점'을 뜻해요. the merits of their case = 그 주장의 실질적 강점.

❌ ① dangers(위험): 무관해요.

❌ ② emotions(감정): 의미가 달라요.

❌ ③ opinions(의견): 주제어를 이용한 함정이에요. merits는 '의견' 자체가 아니라 그 '진가'예요.
det.tip: merits: (주장·사물의) 진가, 장점 ≒ strengths, virtues

questions.passage: There is no problem with people having <u>strong</u> opinions. On the contrary, it’s important that they do and that they argue for them vigorously. However, people’s opinions should always be fact based. Insisting that decision making be fact driven doesn’t detract from the importance of opinions. It just means people are expected to try really hard to make sure theirs are well founded. I often say to executives, “Have an opinion; take a stand; be right most of the time.” Opinions aren’t helpful unless the people who hold them are willing to take a stand in their defense by making a fact-based case. One of the great dangers in business is people who are great at winning an argument due to their powers of persuasion rather than the merits of their case.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 strong과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① weak(약한): strong(강한)의 반의어예요.

❌ ② solid(단단한, 견고한): 오히려 strong과 가까운 뜻이에요.

❌ ③ brief(짧은): 길이에 관한 말로 의미축이 달라요.

❌ ④ honest(정직한): 성격에 관한 말로 무관해요.
det.tip: strong(강한) ↔ weak(약한). solid는 동의어 함정이에요.

questions.passage: There is no problem with people having strong opinions. On the contrary, it’s important that they do and that they argue for them vigorously. However, people’s opinions should always be fact based. Insisting that decision making be fact driven doesn’t detract from the importance of opinions. It just means people are expected to try really hard to make sure theirs are well founded. I often say to executives, “Have an opinion; take a stand; be right most of the time.” Opinions aren’t helpful unless the people who hold them are willing to take a stand in their defense by making a fact-based case. One of the great <u>dangers</u> in business is people who are great at winning an argument due to their powers of persuasion rather than the merits of their case.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 dangers와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ④ benefits(이익, 이점): dangers(위험)의 반의어예요. 위험 ↔ 이익.

❌ ① threats(위협): 위험과 가까운 동의어예요.

❌ ② warnings(경고): 위험을 알리는 것으로 관련이 깊어 반의어가 아니에요.

❌ ③ obstacles(장애물): 부정적 의미라 반의어가 아니에요.
det.tip: dangers(위험) ↔ benefits(이익). threats/warnings/obstacles는 모두 부정적이라 반의어가 아니에요.

questions.passage:
(A) The lawyer built a convincing <u>case</u> to defend her client in court.

(B) He carefully placed the violin back into its velvet <u>case</u> after the concert.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)의 밑줄 친 case의 문맥적 의미로 가장 적절하게 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② (A) 주장 — (B) 상자

(A) 변호사가 법정에서 의뢰인을 변호하기 위해 설득력 있는 '주장(변론)'을 세웠다는 뜻이에요. 본문의 a fact-based case, the merits of their case와 같은 쓰임이에요.

(B) 콘서트 후 바이올린을 벨벳 '케이스(상자)'에 다시 넣었다는 뜻이에요.

❌ ① 두 의미가 서로 뒤바뀌었어요.

❌ ③ '경우/사건'은 두 문맥 모두에 맞지 않아요.

❌ ④ '사건/경우'는 두 문맥 모두에 맞지 않아요.
det.tip: case: ① 주장, 변론, 사례 ② (물건을 넣는) 상자, 케이스

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"the act of making someone believe something or agree to do something by giving them reasons"

det.korean: 이유를 들어 남을 믿게 하거나 동의하게 만드는 행위 = persuasion(설득)
det.analysis:
✅ ③ persuasion(설득): '이유를 들어 남을 믿거나 동의하게 만드는 행위'라는 정의와 일치해요. 본문 powers of persuasion(설득력)에서 쓰였어요.

❌ ① confession(고백): 잘못이나 사실을 털어놓는 것이에요.

❌ ② hesitation(망설임): 결정을 못 하고 머뭇거리는 것이에요.

❌ ④ celebration(축하): 기념하는 행위예요.
det.tip: persuasion: 설득 (persuade 설득하다 + -sion 명사형)

questions.passage: Insisting that decision making be fact driven doesn’t detract from the importance of opinions. It just means people are __________ (expect) to try really hard to make sure theirs are well founded.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: people are __________ (expect) to try really hard.

→ be동사 are 뒤에 오는 자리이고 'people are ~ to'는 '사람들이 ~하도록 기대되다'라는 수동의 뜻이에요.
→ be동사 + 과거분사(p.p.) 수동태이므로 expect를 expected로 바꿔요. be expected to = ~하도록 기대되다.

따라서 정답은 expected예요.
det.tip: be expected to + 동사원형: ~하도록 기대되다 (be + p.p. 수동태)

questions.passage: However, people’s opinions should always be fact based. Insisting that decision making be fact driven doesn’t detract from the __________ (important) of opinions.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: doesn’t detract from the __________ (important) of opinions.

→ 관사 the와 전치사 of 사이는 명사가 오는 자리예요.
→ 형용사 important(중요한)를 명사 importance(중요성)로 바꿔요. the importance of opinions = 의견의 중요성.

따라서 정답은 importance예요.
det.tip: important(형용사: 중요한) → importance(명사: 중요성)

questions.passage: There is no problem with people having strong opinions. On the contrary, it’s important that they do and that they argue for them vigorously. However, people’s opinions should always be fact based. Insisting that decision making be fact driven doesn’t detract from the importance of opinions. It just means people are expected to try really hard to make sure theirs are well founded. I often say to executives, “Have an opinion; take a stand; be right most of the time.” Opinions aren’t helpful unless the people who hold them are willing to __________ by making a fact-based case. One of the great dangers in business is people who are great at winning an argument due to their powers of persuasion rather than the merits of their case.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸: take a stand in their defense(그것을 옹호하며 입장을 견지하다)
det.analysis:
✅ ① take a stand in their defense(그것을 옹호하며 입장을 견지하다): 의견은 그것을 가진 사람이 '기꺼이 나서서 옹호하며 입장을 견지'하고 사실 근거를 제시할 때에만 유용하다는 흐름이에요.

❌ ② hide behind vague words(모호한 말 뒤에 숨다): 옹호에 나선다는 능동적 태도와 반대예요.

❌ ③ avoid any real debate(진짜 논쟁을 피하다): 나서서 주장하라는 글의 취지와 모순이에요.

❌ ④ ignore all the evidence(모든 증거를 무시하다): 사실 근거를 제시하라는 내용과 정반대예요.
det.tip: take a stand in one’s defense: ~을 옹호하며 입장을 견지하다

ch: take a stand in their defense

questions.passage: There is no problem with people having strong opinions. On the contrary, it’s important that they do and that they argue for them vigorously. However, people’s opinions should always be fact based. Insisting that decision making be fact driven doesn’t detract from the importance of opinions. It just means people are expected to try really hard to make sure theirs are well founded. I often say to executives, “Have an opinion; take a stand; be right most of the time.” Opinions aren’t helpful unless the people who hold them are willing to take a stand in their defense by making a fact-based case. One of the great dangers in business is people who are great at winning an argument due to their __________ rather than the merits of their case.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ④ the powers of persuasion(설득력): 사업의 큰 위험은 주장의 '진가(merits)'가 아니라 '설득력'만으로 논쟁에서 이기는 사람들이라는 대비예요. rather than the merits of their case(그들 주장의 진가가 아니라)와 짝을 이뤄요.

❌ ① the strength of their evidence(증거의 힘): 오히려 글이 바람직하게 보는 '사실 근거'라 위험의 원인이 될 수 없어요.

❌ ② the depth of their research(연구의 깊이): 본문에 없는 내용이에요.

❌ ③ the years of their practice(수년간의 연습): 본문과 무관해요.
det.tip: win due to powers of persuasion rather than the merits: 진가가 아니라 설득력으로 이기다
